title: Capacity Chaos Camp: Controlled Experimentation & Triage Handbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

Purpose: This handbook defines a safe, repeatable process for running focused capacity experiments (the "Capacity Chaos Camp") against production-adjacent environments. The goals are to validate autoscaler behavior, eviction/fallback policies, prefetch/policy warmup, and cross-tenant degradation modes without endangering customer SLAs.

Audience: platform operators, experiment owners, SREs, and platform engineers running controlled capacity/chaos tests.

High-level approach:
- Run in progressively wider cohorts (canary -> regional sandbox -> limited-production slice).
- Enforce safety gates before each escalation.
- Pair every experiment with a rollback playbook and a postmortem and metrics review.

Scope and out-of-scope

In-scope:
- Autoscaler behavior under synthetic load (scale up, scale down, oscillation).
- KV/prefix cache eviction and warmset re-population.
- Tenant burst scenarios and burst-credit economics validation.
- Model-variant fallback and routing under constrained capacity.
- Prefetch and batching performance under varying hotset sizes.

Out-of-scope (do not run as part of Chaos Camp):
- Actions that modify customer data sets or deletes.
- Tests that require network segmentation changes in customer VPCs.
- Rolling kernel upgrades across all GPU hosts (use maintenance runbooks instead).

Roles & responsibilities

- Experiment Owner (EO) — defines hypothesis, plan, success criteria, and coordinates schedule. (example: @e.caldwell)
- Run Lead — executes prechecks, triggers experiment steps, owns rollback.
- Observation Lead — owns dashboards and alert channels during the run.
- Pager/Oncall — SRE on duty who can approve rollback and engage engineers.
- Postmortem Owner — collects data, writes follow-up, and drives remediation.

Safety gates (preconditions)

Every experiment must pass the following checks before running in any environment: 
1) Business approval: product or customer success signoff if experiment touches customer-visible SLAs.
2) Capacity isolation: a scoped set of tenants (tenant IDs listed) or a dedicated sandbox cluster must be reserved.
3) Backup snapshots: KV prefix cache and metering snapshots taken within the last 30 minutes.
4) Operator staffing: Run Lead, Observation Lead, and Pager present for the window.
5) Telemetry baseline: 24h baseline of SLI/SLO metrics captured and stored as a named query.
6) Rollback plan: clear automated and manual rollback steps defined and smoke-tested in staging.

Experiment design checklist

- Hypothesis (1 sentence): e.g., "Increasing per-tenant ephemeral batch size by 2x will not increase 99th-percentile foreground latency by >20% for tiered tenants."
- Independent variable(s): batch size, eviction threshold, prefetch concurrency, autoscaler delta.
- Dependent metrics: p50/p95/p99 foreground latency, token cost-per-request, eviction rate, request error rate, SLO burn percentage.
- Safety thresholds (hard stop): p99 latency > 2x baseline, error rate > 1%, eviction rate > 30% sustained for 5 min.
- Escalation contacts and communication channel (Slack, PagerDuty, incident bridge).
- Duration and rollback window.

Telemetry & dashboards to watch

Create a dedicated experiment dashboard with the following panels (minimum):
- Global latent metrics: p50/p95/p99 end-to-end foreground token latency (by tenant slice).
- Token cost rate: tokens/sec and cost-per-token approximation by model variant.
- Eviction metrics: KV eviction/sec, cold-cache-miss-rate.
- Autoscaler signals: desired_replicas, current_replicas, scale_events, scaling_latency.
- Queue backpressure: request queue length, average queue time, rejection rate.
- Operator signals: number of active prefetch workers, kernel-switch events, GPU temp/PCI errors.

Recommended alert thresholds (examples)

- p99 latency: warn at 1.5x baseline for 10m, critical at 2x baseline for 5m.
- Request error rate: warn at 0.5% 5m, critical at 1% 3m.
- Eviction rate: warn at 20% sustained 10m, critical at 30% sustained 5m.
- Autoscaler flapping: >3 scale events per 10m -> automatic pause of experiment and operator review.

Experiment runbook (step-by-step)

Pre-run (T-72h -> T-1h):
1) EO publishes experiment PRD in the experiment backlog and tags reviewers.
2) Reserve sandbox capacity and configure tenant slice.
3) Create named telemetry baselines and dashboard.
4) Run smoke exercise in staging to validate rollback scripts.
5) Final safety-gate check at T-1h and Slack channel creation (#chaos-camp-YYYYMMDD).

Execution (T0 -> T+window):
1) Run Lead signals start on Slack and records timestamp.
2) Apply independent variable (feature flag, config change, CLI). Example CLI: 
   - rdxctl experiment apply --target tenant-slice=chaos-camp-12 --config batch-size=2048 --run-id=camp-2025-09-10
3) Observation Lead monitors dashboards and logs for early signs.
4) If any hard-stop threshold breaches, Run Lead executes rollback (see rollback procedure).
5) If warnings trigger, engage Pager and optionally pause escalation.
6) At midpoint, record intermediate metrics snapshot and produce quick status update.
7) At window end, revert changes and perform smoke validation that baseline behavior resumes.

Rollback procedure (immediate actions)

1) Run Lead issues "ROLLBACK" on the Slack channel and toggles the pre-tested rollback script: 
   - rdxctl experiment rollback --run-id=camp-2025-09-10 --scope tenant-slice=chaos-camp-12
2) Scale policies: set back-off to conservative defaults, reduce prefetch concurrency to 1.
3) If automated rollback fails, operator executes manual steps (pin model variant, redirect routing to fallback region).
4) Observation Lead continues to monitor and confirm stabilization (p99 within 1.2x baseline and error rate <0.2%).
5) Run Lead opens incident if rollback did not resolve within 15 minutes.

Triage and mitigation flow (short form)

1) Identify symptom: latency spike / error increase / eviction surge.
2) Map to likely cause: scaling, cache eviction, prefetch overload, kernel switch, hardware degradation.
3) Run quick isolation: reduce independent variable (e.g., revert batch size), throttle tenant slice, or pause prefetchers.
4) If cause unclear, run targeted diagnostic queries (examples in Appendix).
5) If cross-tenant impact, immediately engage product CS to inform customers and open incident.

Post-experiment analysis and postmortem template

Required deliverables within 72h:
- Experimental PRD link and run-id.
- Raw telemetry export for the run window (timestamped).
- Summary of deviations from baseline and hypothesis verdict (pass/fail).
- List of any safety gate violations and timeline of operator actions.
- Action items with owners and target completion dates.

Postmortem template fields:
- Title, Run ID, Experiment Owner, Run Lead, Observation Lead, Pager, Start/End times.
- Hypothesis and intended change.
- Metrics comparison (table): baseline vs during-run vs after-roll-back.
- Root cause analysis and evidence.
- Remediation plan and rollout guidance for production.

Success criteria and metrics for experiment graduation

- No critical SLO breaches during cohort windows across two independent runs.
- Predictable autoscale behavior: scale latency within target +/- 15% and no oscillation.
- Eviction and cold-miss rates within acceptable band (documented per-model thresholds).
- Positive cost-performance tradeoff validated: token cost delta measured and approved by cost-ops.

Scheduling, stakeholder communication, and approvals

- Book a 1-hour pre-run sync (EO, Run Lead, Observation Lead, SRE pager) 24h prior.
- Notify CS and sales if experiment may affect paying customers; provide scheduled maintenance window.
- Post-run review with stakeholders within 5 business days.

Appendix: query and CLI snippets

Prometheus example (p99 latency query):
  histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="foreground"}[5m])) by (le))

Eviction rate example (PromQL):
  sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[1m])) by (shard) / sum(kv_items_total) by (shard)

rdxctl example commands:
  rdxctl experiment apply --target tenant-slice=chaos-camp-12 --config batch-size=2048 --run-id=camp-2025-09-10
  rdxctl experiment rollback --run-id=camp-2025-09-10 --scope tenant-slice=chaos-camp-12

End of handbook.
